analyzed_vuln.description: `blosc_d` trusts metadata-derived `src_offset/srcsize` for lazy chunks and then performs `cbytes = sw32_(src)` without ensuring `src` still points inside the actual chunk buffer. In the lazy path (`is_lazy`), `block_csize` is read from trailer metadata and used to set `srcsize`, but `src_offset` can be inconsistent/too large relative to real loaded data, causing `src += src_offset` to move out of bounds while `srcsize` bookkeeping still appears valid. The subsequent 4-byte read in `sw32_` becomes a heap OOB read.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In `decompress_frame_fuzzer`, attacker-controlled frame/chunk bytes must parse far enough to reach `frame_decompress_chunk -> blosc2_decompress_ctx -> blosc_d` with lazy-chunk handling enabled. Crafted chunk/trailer fields (notably block size/offset metadata) must make `blosc_d` accept the state and enter the stream loop with an invalid `src` pointer but nonnegative `srcsize` check, so `sw32_(src)` reads 4 bytes past the allocated input buffer.
